references.text: Jacob's family mourns for him with great grief, mirroring the deep sorrow Jacob himself showed when he thought Joseph was dead.
Jacob refuses to send Benjamin to Egypt and says he will go down to Sheol in grief if anything happens to him – a direct echo of the words in 37:35.
Judah repeats Jacob's words that he will go down to Sheol in grief, directly referring to Jacob's inconsolable sorrow over Joseph.
David mourns inconsolably for Absalom's death and refuses to be comforted, mirroring Jacob's refusal to be comforted after Joseph's presumed death.
Rachel weeps for her children and refuses to be comforted, reminiscent of Jacob's inconsolable grief over Joseph.
Judah's warning about the father's fate confirms that the threat in 37:35 was meant literally and shows the consequence of loss.
Jeremiah's instruction to weep over the one 'taken away' highlights the irony in Jacob's sorrow: he weeps for Joseph as if he were dead, while he is actually 'taken away' to Egypt.
Judah's fear of meeting his father without Benjamin is the direct practical unfolding of the threat about 'gray hair going down to the grave' from 37:35.
